note: The District is a single jurisdiction: the 2017 DC Construction Codes (Title 12 DCMR) are both the state-level and the city-level code for Washington, DC. There is no separate city amendment layer.

governing_table.code: 2017 District of Columbia Building Code (2015 International Building Code as amended by 12-A DCMR), Chapter 29. The same table is Table 403.1 of the 2017 District of Columbia Plumbing Code (2015 International Plumbing Code as amended by 12-F DCMR).
governing_table.edition: 2017 DC Construction Codes, in effect since May 29, 2020
governing_table.table: Table 2902.1, Minimum Number of Required Plumbing Fixtures (Plumbing Code Table 403.1)
governing_table.quote: 2902.1 Minimum number of fixtures. Plumbing fixtures shall be provided in the minimum number as shown in Table 2902.1 based on the actual use of the building or space. Uses not shown in Table 2902.1 shall be considered individually by the code official. The number of occupants shall be determined by this code.
governing_table.note: Read in DOB's own integrated PDF of the 2017 Building Code (Part 3, pages 643 to 647). DOB warns that the integrated PDFs do not show amendments adopted after May 29, 2020. The plumbing code copy on UpCodes (secondary) shows the same rows today.

fixtures.cities_may_amend_note: Not applicable: the District has no cities or counties below it. The DC Construction Codes are the only layer. Federal buildings in the District are outside this research.

office.row_label: 2 Business, B: Buildings for the transaction of business, professional services, other services involving merchandise, office buildings, banks, light industrial and similar uses
office.wc_male: 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50
office.wc_female: 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50
office.urinals: Urinals see Section 419.2 of the Plumbing Code (optional substitution, not more than 50 percent)
office.quote: Business B Buildings for the transaction of business, professional services, other services involving merchandise, office buildings, banks, light industrial and similar uses: [water closets, one figure across the male and female columns] 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50; [lavatories] 1 per 40 for the first 80 and 1 per 80 for the remainder exceeding 80

restaurant.row_label: 1 Assembly, A-2: Restaurants, banquet halls and food courts
restaurant.urinals: Urinals see Section 419.2 of the Plumbing Code (optional substitution, not more than 67 percent)
restaurant.quote: A-2 ... Restaurants, banquet halls and food courts: 1 per 75 [male] 1 per 75 [female]; [lavatories] 1 per 200. Footnote d (on A-2): The occupant load for seasonal outdoor seating and entertainment areas shall be included when determining the minimum number of facilities required.

school.urinals: Urinals see Section 419.2 of the Plumbing Code (optional substitution, not more than 67 percent)
school.quote: Educational E Educational facilities: [water closets] 1 per 50; [lavatories] 1 per 50

sex_split.text: Divide the total occupant load in half, unless approved statistical data show a different split.
sex_split.quote: 2902.1.1 Fixture calculations. To determine the occupant load of each sex, the total occupant load shall be divided in half. ... Exception: The total occupant load shall not be required to be divided in half where approved statistical data indicate a distribution of the sexes of other than 50 percent of each sex.

rounding.text: Any fraction rounds up to the next whole fixture. With several occupancies, add the fractions first, then round up.
rounding.quote: Fractional numbers resulting from applying the fixture ratios of Table 2902.1 shall be rounded up to the next whole number. For calculations involving multiple occupancies, such fractional numbers for each occupancy shall first be summed and then rounded up to the next whole number. [Table footnote a] The fixtures shown are based on one fixture being the minimum required for the number of persons indicated or any fraction of the number of persons indicated.

urinal_substitution.text: Urinals are optional. In each toilet room they may replace up to 67 percent of the required toilets in assembly and educational occupancies (restaurants, schools) and up to 50 percent in all other occupancies (offices). The code does not say how a fraction of a urinal rounds; the worked examples round down because the text says "not more than". Each urinal needs a privacy screen on each side.
urinal_substitution.quote: [Plumbing Code] 419.2 Substitution for Water Closets. In each bathroom or toilet room, urinals shall not be substituted for more than 67 percent of the required water closets in assembly and educational occupancies. Urinals shall not be substituted for more than 50 percent of the required water closets in all other occupancies. [Building Code] 1210.3.2 Urinal partitions. Each urinal utilized by the public or employees shall occupy a separate area with walls or partitions to provide privacy. The walls or partitions shall begin at a height not more than 12 inches (305 mm) from and extend not less than 60 inches (1524 mm) above the finished floor surface.
urinal_substitution.source_note: Section 419.2 was read on UpCodes (secondary copy of the 2017 DC Plumbing Code). The building code table header points to it: "URINALS SEE SECTION 419.2 OF THE PLUMBING CODE" (official PDF). Section 1210.3.2 was read in the official PDF, Part 1.

small_occupancy_exception.text: Separate men's and women's rooms are not required where the total occupant load, employees and customers together, is 15 or fewer; in shops (mercantile) with an occupant load of 100 or less; or, by a District amendment, in a building or tenant space that provides single-occupancy gender-neutral toilet rooms. Where each sex needs only one toilet, two family or assisted-use rooms may serve instead.
small_occupancy_exception.quote: 2902.2 Separate facilities. Where plumbing fixtures are required, separate facilities shall be provided for each sex. Exceptions: 1. Separate facilities shall not be required for dwelling units and sleeping units. 2. Separate facilities shall not be required in structures or tenant spaces with a total occupant load, including both employees and customers, of 15 or fewer. 3. Separate facilities shall not be required in mercantile occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 100 or less. 4. Separate facilities shall not be required in buildings or tenant spaces where single-occupancy gender-neutral public toilet facilities are provided in accordance with Section 2902.4. 2902.2.1 ... Where a building or tenant space requires a separate toilet facility for each sex and each toilet facility is required to have only one water closet, two family or assisted-use toilet facilities shall be permitted to serve as the required separate facilities.

occupant_load.text: Office (business areas): 100 square feet gross per person. Restaurant dining room (assembly without fixed seats, unconcentrated, tables and chairs): 15 square feet net. Classroom: 20 square feet net. The District is on the 2015 model code, so the office figure is 100, not the 150 of later editions.
occupant_load.quote: TABLE 1004.1.2 MAXIMUM FLOOR AREA ALLOWANCES PER OCCUPANT ... Assembly without fixed seats: Concentrated (chairs only, not fixed) 7 net; Standing space 5 net; Unconcentrated (tables and chairs) 15 net ... Business areas 100 gross ... Educational: Classroom area 20 net
occupant_load.source_note: Official PDF, Part 1. The PDF's text layer misaligns the three assembly figures; the order 7, 5, 15 was confirmed on UpCodes' copy of the 2017 DC Building Code, Chapter 10.

worked_examples.how: 25 women and 25 men. 25 / 25 = 1 each. Half of 1 is less than one fixture, so no urinal may replace the only toilet.
50 each. First 50 at 1 per 25 = 2 each. Urinals: not more than 50% of 2 = 1.
100 each. First 50 = 2, remaining 50 at 1 per 50 = 1, total 3 each. Urinals: 50% of 3 = 1.5, so 1.
200 each. First 50 = 2, remaining 150 at 1 per 50 = 3, total 5 each. Urinals: 50% of 5 = 2.5, so 2.
25 each. 25 / 75 = 0.33, rounds up to 1 each. 67% of 1 is less than one fixture, so no urinal substitution.
50 each. 50 / 75 = 0.67, rounds up to 1 each. No urinal substitution.
100 each. 100 / 75 = 1.33, rounds up to 2 each. Urinals: 67% of 2 = 1.34, so 1.
200 each. 200 / 75 = 2.67, rounds up to 3 each. Urinals: 67% of 3 = 2.01, so 2.
25 each. 25 / 50 = 0.5, rounds up to 1 each. No urinal substitution.

fixtures.worked_examples_note: Urinal figures assume one men's room; Section 419.2 applies the limit "in each bathroom or toilet room". Rounding the urinal fraction down is this file's reading, not a stated rule.

hdpe_fire.section: 2017 DC Building Code Section 803.9 (unamended from the 2015 IBC), which points to the room-corner test of Section 803.1.2 (NFPA 286). Toilet room privacy partitions are interior wall finish by the Chapter 2 definition.
hdpe_fire.quote: 803.9 High-density polyethylene (HDPE) and polypropylene (PP). Where high-density polyethylene or polypropylene is used as an interior finish it shall comply with Section 803.1.2. | 803.1.2 Room corner test for interior wall or ceiling finish materials. Interior wall or ceiling finish materials shall be permitted to be tested in accordance with NFPA 286. Interior wall or ceiling finish materials tested in accordance with NFPA 286 shall comply with Section 803.1.2.1. | [Chapter 2] INTERIOR WALL AND CEILING FINISH. The exposed interior surfaces of buildings, including but not limited to: fixed or movable walls and partitions; toilet room privacy partitions; columns; ceilings ...

access.state_standard: Chapter 11 of the 2017 DC Building Code (2015 IBC Chapter 11 as amended) with ICC A117.1-2009 as the technical standard ("Buildings and facilities shall be designed and constructed to be accessible in accordance with this code and ICC A117.1"; referenced standards list: "ICC A117.1-09"). The federal 2010 ADA Standards apply alongside. A117.1-2009 Chapter 6 was read on UpCodes' copy ("District of Columbia Accessibility Code 2009"), a secondary source.

differences.point: Vertical grab bar beside the toilet in accessible stalls
differences.state: A117.1-2009 604.5.1 adds an 18-inch vertical grab bar on the side wall, in addition to the horizontal side and rear bars (604.9.6 applies 604.5.1 to wheelchair stalls, 604.10.4 to ambulatory stalls).
differences.federal: 2010 ADA Standards 604.5.1: "The side wall grab bar shall be 42 inches (1065 mm) long minimum, located 12 inches (305 mm) maximum from the rear wall and extending 54 inches (1370 mm) minimum from the rear wall." No vertical bar.
differences.quote: 604.5.1 Fixed Side Wall Grab Bars. Fixed side-wall grab bars shall be 42 inches (1065 mm) minimum in length, located 12 inches (305 mm) maximum from the rear wall and extending 54 inches (1370 mm) minimum from the rear wall. In addition, a vertical grab bar 18 inches (455 mm) minimum in length shall be mounted with the bottom of the bar located 39 inches (990 mm) minimum and 41 inches (1040 mm) maximum above the floor, and with the center line of the bar located 39 inches (990 mm) minimum and 41 inches (1040 mm) maximum from the rear wall.

differences.federal: 2010 ADA Standards 604.8.2.1: "Ambulatory accessible compartments shall have a depth of 60 inches (1525 mm) minimum and a width of 35 inches (890 mm) minimum and 37 inches (940 mm) maximum."
differences.quote: 604.10.2 Size. The minimum area of an ambulatory accessible compartment shall be 60 inches (1525 mm) minimum in depth and 36 inches (915 mm) in width.

differences.state: At least 5 percent of the compartments in a room must be wheelchair accessible, and 5 percent ambulatory where stalls plus urinals total six or more. In rooms of up to 20 stalls this gives the same count as the federal rule; it adds stalls only in very large rooms.
differences.federal: 2010 ADA Standards 213.3.1: "Where toilet compartments are provided, at least one toilet compartment shall comply with 604.8.1. In addition to the compartment required to comply with 604.8.1, at least one compartment shall comply with 604.8.2 where six or more toilet compartments are provided, or where the combination of urinals and water closets totals six or more fixtures."
differences.quote: 1109.2.2 Water closet compartment. Where water closet compartments are provided in a toilet room or bathing room, at least 5 percent of the total number of compartments shall be wheelchair accessible. Where the combined total water closet compartments and urinals provided in a toilet room or bathing room is six or more, at least 5 percent of the total number of compartments shall be ambulatory accessible, provided in addition to the wheelchair-accessible compartment.

differences.point: Family or assisted-use toilet room in assembly and mercantile buildings
differences.state: Required where six or more toilets in total (men's plus women's) are required in an assembly or mercantile occupancy, restaurants included. The room has one toilet and one sink and a door that locks from inside.
differences.federal: The 2010 ADA Standards have no requirement to add a family or unisex room in new work; 213.2.1 only describes one ("Unisex toilet rooms shall contain not more than one lavatory, and two water closets without urinals or one water closet and one urinal").
differences.quote: 1109.2.1 Family or assisted-use toilet and bathing rooms. In assembly and mercantile occupancies, an accessible family or assisted-use toilet room shall be provided where an aggregate of six or more male and female water closets is required.

differences.point: Toilet paper dispenser position (affects where it mounts on the partition)
differences.state: A117.1-2009 measures from the rear wall: outlet 24 to 36 inches from the rear wall if above the grab bar, 24 to 42 inches if below, and 18 to 48 inches above the floor.
differences.federal: 2010 ADA Standards 604.7: "Toilet paper dispensers shall comply with 309.4 and shall be 7 inches (180 mm) minimum and 9 inches (230 mm) maximum in front of the water closet measured to the centerline of the dispenser. The outlet of the dispenser shall be 15 inches (380 mm) minimum and 48 inches (1220 mm) maximum above the finish floor and shall not be located behind grab bars."
differences.quote: 604.7 Dispensers. Toilet paper dispensers shall comply with Section 309.4. Where the dispenser is located above the grab bar, the outlet of the dispenser shall be located within an area 24 inches (610 mm) minimum and 36 inches (915 mm) maximum from the rear wall. Where the dispenser is located below the grab bar, the outlet of the dispenser shall be located within an area 24 inches (610 mm) minimum and 42 inches (1065 mm) maximum from the rear wall. The outlet of the dispenser shall be located 18 inches (455 mm) minimum and 48 inches (1220 mm) maximum above the floor.

differences.point: Wheelchair stall door position: an extra option, not a stricter rule
differences.state: A117.1-2009 Table 604.9.3.1 also allows a front door opening at least 56 inches from the side wall nearest the toilet, as an alternative to 4 inches maximum from the far side. A layout using only this alternative may not meet the federal text.
differences.federal: 2010 ADA Standards 604.8.1.2: "Doors shall be located in the front partition or in the side wall or partition farthest from the water closet. Where located in the front partition, the door opening shall be 4 inches (100 mm) maximum from the side wall or partition farthest from the water closet."
differences.quote: TABLE 604.9.3.1 DOOR OPENING LOCATION. Front Wall or Partition: From the side wall or partition closest to the water closet 56 inches (1420 mm) minimum or From the side wall or partition farthest from the water closet 4 inches (100 mm) maximum

differences.state: Single-occupancy public toilet rooms must have gender-neutral signs; multi-occupancy rooms are signed for each sex (District amendment to Section 2902.4).
differences.federal: The 2010 ADA Standards regulate how signs are made and placed (section 703, section 216), not whether a room is designated by sex.
differences.quote: 2902.4 Signage. Multi-occupancy public toilet facilities shall be designated by a legible sign for each sex. Single-occupancy public facilities shall be designated with gender-neutral signage. Signs shall be readily visible and located near the entrance to each toilet facility. Signs for accessible toilet facilities shall comply with Section 1111.

access.same_as_federal: Wheelchair stall size (60 inches wide, 56 deep wall-hung or 59 floor-mounted), toe clearance (9 inches, 12 for children), self-closing door with pulls both sides, and children's stall rules read the same in A117.1-2009 sections 604.9 to 604.11 and 2010 ADA Standards 604.8 to 604.9.
access.process: No separate District accessibility registration or state-level review step was found. Chapter 11 is part of the Building Code, which the DC Department of Buildings (DOB) applies when it reviews permit plans. Not read: DOB's permit pages on what a partition replacement triggers.

single_user.rule: Single-occupancy public restrooms must carry gender-neutral signs, under both the DC Building and Plumbing Codes and the DC human rights regulations (4 DCMR 802.2, enforced by the Office of Human Rights). A building or tenant space that provides single-occupancy gender-neutral rooms does not need separate men's and women's rooms.
single_user.quote: [Building Code 2902.4] Single-occupancy public facilities shall be designated with gender-neutral signage. [2902.2 exception 4] Separate facilities shall not be required in buildings or tenant spaces where single-occupancy gender-neutral public toilet facilities are provided in accordance with Section 2902.4. [OHR, Safe Bathrooms DC] In the District of Columbia, we are attempting to reduce that stress by making every single-stall public bathroom in the District gender-neutral. It's the law, D.C. Mun. Regs. tit. 4. § 802.2 (2006) ... To make a single-stall bathroom compliant, all that is needed is a sign that says "Restroom," or something similar, to indicate it is gender-neutral.

all_gender_shared.rule: The 2017 DC codes do not provide for a shared all-gender room with several stalls. Where fixtures are required, separate facilities for each sex are required unless an exception applies (15 or fewer occupants, small shops, or single-occupancy gender-neutral rooms), and multi-occupancy rooms must be signed for each sex. A shared multi-stall all-gender room would need DOB's approval as a code modification: ask DOB. Every toilet must be in its own compartment with a door, and every urinal screened, in any case.
all_gender_shared.quote: 2902.2 Separate facilities. Where plumbing fixtures are required, separate facilities shall be provided for each sex. ... 2902.4 Signage. Multi-occupancy public toilet facilities shall be designated by a legible sign for each sex. | 1210.3.1 Water closet compartment. Each water closet utilized by the public or employees shall occupy a separate compartment with walls or partitions and a door enclosing the fixtures to ensure privacy. | [OHR release, March 4, 2011] Multiple-stall restrooms may continue to be gender segregated.

use_restrictions.rule: No District law restricting restroom use by sex was found. The District's human rights regulations go the other way: 4 DCMR 802 ("Restrooms and other gender specific facilities", in the chapter on gender identity or expression) is the rule OHR enforces. The text of 802.1 (use of gender-specific facilities consistent with gender identity) could not be opened on dcregs.dc.gov and is known here only from a search result, so it is not quoted.
use_restrictions.quote: [dcregs.dc.gov rule record] Section: 4-802 RESTROOMS AND OTHER GENDER SPECIFIC FACILITIES. Title: 4 HUMAN RIGHTS AND RELATIONS. Chapter: 4-8 COMPLIANCE RULES AND REGULATIONS REGARDING GENDER IDENTITY OR EXPRESSION. Source: Final Rulemaking published at 53 DCR 8751, 8753 (October 27, 2006).

public_wage.law: No District prevailing wage statute for construction was found. The federal Davis-Bacon Act names the District directly: it covers construction contracts over $2,000 to which the District of Columbia is a party, so District government building work (schools, city buildings) carries the U.S. Department of Labor's wage determination for the District.
public_wage.quote: 40 U.S.C. 3142(a) Application. The advertised specifications for every contract in excess of $2,000, to which the Federal Government or the District of Columbia is a party, for construction, alteration, or repair, including painting and decorating, of public buildings and public works of the Government or the District of Columbia that are located in a State or the District of Columbia and which requires or involves the employment of mechanics or laborers shall contain a provision stating the minimum wages to be paid various classes of laborers and mechanics. (b) Based on Prevailing Wage. The minimum wages shall be based on the wages the Secretary of Labor determines to be prevailing ... in the District of Columbia if the work is to be performed there.
public_wage.note: Statute read on Cornell LII (secondary copy of the U.S. Code); dol.gov returned Access Denied. The DC building wage determination number on sam.gov was not looked up: the city agent adds the carpenter rate.

sales_tax.rate_note: 6.0% before October 1, 2027 and 7.0% from October 1, 2027 (D.C. Code 47-2002(a) and 47-2202(a)). There are no local add-on rates in the District.

shipped_goods.rule: Partitions delivered in the District are taxable at 6%. A seller with no physical presence must collect once its retail sales delivered into the District exceed $100,000 or reach 200 separate sales in the current or previous calendar year. If the seller doesn't collect, the buyer owes use tax at the same rate.
shipped_goods.quote: [D.C. Code 47-2001(w)] "Vendor" includes a person or retailer selling property or rendering services upon the receipts from which a tax is imposed under this chapter, including a person or retailer that does not have a physical presence in the District that in the previous calendar year or the current calendar year had gross receipts from all retail sales delivered into the District that exceeds $100,000 or 200 or more separate retail sales delivered into the District. [OTR FAQ] The use tax is a tax imposed at the same rate as the sales tax. It is imposed on the purchase or rental of tangible personal property that will be used, stored or consumed in the District by a buyer who did not pay sales tax to the District or any other taxing jurisdiction at the time of the purchase or rental.

freight.rule: Depends on the invoice. The sales price leaves out "transportation charges separately stated, if the transportation occurs after the sale of the property is made"; transportation cost before the sale can't be deducted. Separately, a delivery charge is itself a taxable service only where pick-up and delivery are both in the District (OTR's 2010 guide), which a shipment from an out-of-state plant is not. OTR has no page that applies this to freight on an interstate shipment.
freight.quote: [47-2001(p)(1)] "Sales price" means the total amount paid by a purchaser to a vendor ... without any deduction on account of ... (C) The cost of transportation of the property prior to its sale at retail. [47-2001(p)(2)] The term "sales price" does not include ... (E) Transportation charges separately stated, if the transportation occurs after the sale of the property is made. [47-2001(n)(1)(Q)] The sale of or charge for any delivery in the District for which a separate charge is made, except merchandise delivered for resale ... [OTR FR-379, 2010] Charges for any delivery where pick up and delivery is in the District for which a separate charge is made

install_labor.rule: Installation labor billed separately is left out of the taxed price. The exception is work that counts as a taxable service: "real property maintenance" (minor adjustments, maintenance or repairs that keep a building functional) is taxed at 6%, but services performed as part of construction or major repairs are not.
install_labor.quote: [47-2001(p)(2)] The term "sales price" does not include ... (C) The amount separately charged for labor or services rendered in installing or applying the property sold, except as provided in subsection (n)(1) of this section. [47-2001(n)(1)(M)] ... "real property maintenance" means any activity that keeps the land or the premises of a building clean, orderly, and functional, including the performance of minor adjustments, maintenance, or repairs ... but does not include; painting, wallpapering, or other services performed as part of construction or major repairs. [OTR FR-800 instructions, 2026] Sales price does not include: (1) cash discounts allowed and taken on sales; (2) separately stated initial installation charges; and (3) sales tax collected by the vendor from the purchaser.

furnish_and_install.rule: The sale of materials for construction, repair or alteration of real property, which become real property when the work is done, is itself the taxable retail sale: the contractor pays tax when buying the materials. Whether installed toilet partitions "become real property", and how the contractor then bills the customer, is not stated in what was read (9 DCMR chapter 4 was not read).
furnish_and_install.quote: [47-2001(n)(1)(E)] The sale of material used in the construction, and of materials used in the repair or alteration, of real property, which materials, upon completion of such construction, alterations, or repairs, become real property, regardless of whether or not such real property is to be sold or resold ...

sales_tax.agency: DC Office of Tax and Revenue (OTR)

page.stalls_intro: DC counts toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. It isn't the number of staff or of visitors in a day. Half are counted as men and half as women. Every toilet needs a stall, and every urinal needs a screen on each side. Urinals are optional: in a men's room they may replace up to half of the toilets in an office and up to two thirds in a restaurant or school, so the table shows the men's side as stalls.
page.stalls_after: These are minimums for the whole building, and at least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible. A men's room that needs only one toilet can't swap it for a urinal. A space designed for 15 people or fewer may have one shared restroom, and one-person restrooms open to everyone may take the place of separate men's and women's rooms.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, DC's building rules count an office at one person per 100 square feet of floor, a restaurant dining room at one per 15 square feet and a classroom at one per 20.
page.fire_bullet: - **Fire safety:** DC's building rules require solid plastic (HDPE) partitions to pass a room-corner fire test. Ask for the fire-rated version.
page.access_bullet: - **Wheelchair access:** a restroom with stalls needs at least one stall a wheelchair user can enter and use, and a room with six or more stalls and urinals also needs a narrower stall with grab bars on both sides. Federal law and DC's own building rules set the sizes, and the DC Department of Buildings applies them when it reviews permit plans.
page.state_extra_bullet: - **DC extras:** DC's rules add an 18-inch vertical grab bar beside the toilet in accessible stalls, which the federal rules don't require, and set the narrower stall at 36 inches wide. A restaurant, store or other public venue that needs six or more toilets in total must also have a one-person family restroom.
page.restroom_bullet: - **Single-user and all-gender restrooms:** in DC a one-person public restroom must have a gender-neutral sign, such as "Restroom". A building may provide one-person restrooms open to everyone in place of separate men's and women's rooms. Rooms with several stalls are signed for men or women, and DC's building rules don't describe a shared all-gender room with stalls, so ask the DC Department of Buildings before planning one.
page.public_jobs: On District government construction contracts over $2,000, schools and city buildings included, federal law requires at least the wage the U.S. Department of Labor sets for Washington, DC.
page.tax_install_bullet: - **Tax on installation:** in DC, installation labor is left out of the taxed price when it is listed separately on the invoice. Minor repair and maintenance work on a building is taxed as a service, but work done as part of construction or major repairs is not. A contractor who supplies materials that become part of the building pays the tax when buying them.
page.tax_ship_bullet: - **Buying without installation:** partitions shipped to {city} are taxable. A freight charge listed separately on the invoice is left out of the taxed price when the shipping happens after the sale. If the seller doesn't collect the tax, the buyer owes it to the District as use tax.
page.tax_confirm: your accountant or the DC Office of Tax and Revenue

- Toilet counts in DC: 2017 District of Columbia Building Code, Table 2902.1 and Sections 2902.1.1, 2902.2 and 2902.4, in [DOB's integrated code, Part 3](https://dob.dc.gov/sites/default/files/dc/sites/dob/publication/attachments/2017%20District%20of%20Columbia%20Building%20Code_Part3.pdf). Checked 2026-11-24.

- DC stall rules compared with the federal ones: ICC A117.1-2009, Sections 604.5, 604.7, 604.9 and 604.10, read on a secondary copy, [UpCodes, District of Columbia Accessibility Code 2009, Chapter 6](https://up.codes/viewer/district-of-columbia/icc-a117.1-2009/chapter/6/plumbing-elements-and-facilities), and the [2010 ADA Standards](https://www.access-board.gov/ada/), Sections 213 and 604. Checked 2026-11-24.

- Gender-neutral signs on one-person restrooms: 2017 District of Columbia Building Code, Section 2902.4 (link above), and [DC Office of Human Rights, Safe Bathrooms DC](https://ohr.dc.gov/page/safe-bathrooms-dc) (4 DCMR 802.2). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Wages on District government jobs: [40 U.S.C. 3142, Davis-Bacon Act](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/40/3142) (contracts over $2,000 to which the District of Columbia is a party). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Sales tax: [D.C. Code 47-2001](https://code.dccouncil.gov/us/dc/council/code/sections/47-2001) (retail sale, sales price, vendor), [47-2002](https://code.dccouncil.gov/us/dc/council/code/sections/47-2002) and [47-2202](https://code.dccouncil.gov/us/dc/council/code/sections/47-2202) (6% rate, 7% from October 1, 2027); DC Office of Tax and Revenue, [Sales and Use Tax FAQs](https://otr.cfo.dc.gov/page/sales-and-use-tax-faqs), [Taxable and Non-Taxable Services](https://otr.cfo.dc.gov/node/383832) and the [2026 FR-800 Sales and Use Tax instructions](https://mytax.dc.gov/WebFiles/Documents/2026%20FR800MQA%20instructions.pdf). page.official_names: The rules by their official names: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design; ICC A117.1-2009 as referenced by Chapter 11 of the 2017 District of Columbia Building Code; 2017 District of Columbia Building Code (2015 International Building Code as amended by 12-A DCMR), in force since May 29, 2020; 2017 District of Columbia Plumbing Code (2015 International Plumbing Code as amended by 12-F DCMR); 4 DCMR 802 for restroom signs; NFPA 286 for HDPE.

notes: The District's general sales tax rate rises from 6% to 7% on October 1, 2027 (D.C. Code 47-2002(a)). A search result quoting an OTR page gave October 1, 2026; the statute and OTR's Taxable and Non-Taxable Services page, both read on 2026-11-24, say 2027.

The office occupant load factor is 100 square feet gross because the District is still on the 2015 model code; most other packs use 150 (2018 and later editions). An office of the same floor area therefore counts 1.5 times as many people in DC.
DOB's codes page (per the earlier state-codes research) says DOB aims to adopt new construction codes by the end of 2027: recheck every figure here when that happens.
Many Washington buildings are federal. Federal buildings follow federal standards, not the DC Construction Codes; no source was read on this, so it is not in the page text.
